title: Order-Four Symmetry in BGV Bootstrapping: Faster Digit Extraction for Large Primes
authors: Zhenyu Xiong, Mingsheng Wang, Zhedong Wang, and Han Wang
abstract:
Bootstrapping is the computational bottleneck of BGV/BFV fully homomorphic encryption, scaling particularly poorly with large plaintext primes. Its two dominant stages: digit extraction and linear transforms. Recent work has reduced the digit-extraction polynomial degree via null-polynomial lattices and bounded-support constructions, but both evaluate the reduced polynomial via generic Paterson--Stockmeyer at cost $O(\sqrt{d})$ .

  We present two algebraic optimizations that address both stages simultaneously. For digit extraction, we prove that choosing the auxiliary radix $A$ with $A^2\equiv -1\pmod{p}$ induces an order-four character filter, forcing the canonical digit-extraction polynomial to satisfy $P_A(AX)+AP_A(X)=AX$ and eliminating all monomials $X^k$ with $k\not\equiv 1,3\pmod{4}$. The resulting structured decomposition$P_A(X)=\tfrac{1}{2}X+X^3Q(X^4)$ reduces non-scalar multiplications from $O(\sqrt{d})$ to $O(\sqrt{d/r})$. For linear transforms, we provide first concrete instantiation of a Galois-structured mixed-radix butterfly decomposition for non-power-of-two cyclotomics, reducing the automorphism count from $O(\sqrt{D})$ to $O(\log D)$.
  
  On the standard NTT-friendly large-prime set ($p=65537$, $m=2^{16}$, $32768$ slots), our single-threaded \HElib{} implementation achieves a $1.85\times$ digit-extraction speedup ($20.06$s to $10.81$s) and a $1.27\times$ total thin-bootstrapping speedup ($42.3$s to $33.3$s) over the state-of-the-art Ma et al.\ baseline, the three stages the method does not touch moving by at most one per cent. All comparisons are made against the Ma et al.\ baselines, run in the identical pipeline at the same auxiliary radix; across nineteen encrypted parameter sets with $1297\le p\le 65537$, the digit-extraction speedup is $1.72$--$1.88\times$ on general cyclotomic rings ($37637\le m\le 65047$) and $1.84$--$2.13\times$ on the power-of-two ring $m=2^{16}$. Every set we recommend is quoted with concrete bit security.

1     Introduction
Since Gentry introduced the first fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) construc-
tion [10], research in FHE has attracted broad attention and improved several
orders of magnitude in both latency and throughput [3,2,6]. Among the various
FHE schemes, BGV [3] and BFV [2,6] are the most popular for homomorphic
integer arithmetic, offering SIMD functionality in which a plaintext encodes an
array of elements and operations are performed simultaneously on each slot. No-
tably, these schemes follow Gentry’s blueprint where each ciphertext carries noise
that grows during homomorphic evaluation; consequently, evaluating functions
of arbitrary complexity requires bootstrapping, homomorphically evaluating the
decryption circuit to produce a fresh lower-noise ciphertext. The bootstrapping
procedure developed by Halevi and Shoup [13,12] and implemented in HElib is the
foundational blueprint for all subsequent works [4,15,7,16,17]. In practice, poly-
nomial evaluations during bootstrapping account for most of the computational
cost in HElib, which are 3× to 50× more expensive than all other operations
combined [7]. Despite significant progress, BGV bootstrapping remains the main
bottleneck for large plaintext primes p, where the cost scales very poorly [11].

stages that together consume over 99% of the total running time:

1.2       Our Contributions
In this work, we investigate new algebraic techniques to accelerate both dominant
stages of large-prime BGV bootstrapping. We address the fundamental challenge
of reducing homomorphic evaluation cost beyond the information-theoretic de-
gree bound through character-theoretic representation theory and structured
linear-transform decomposition. Our main contributions are summarized below:
1. Character-structured digit-extraction polynomial with optimal eval-
   uation cost. We introduce a novel construction that exploits the order-4
   cyclic symmetry of the bounded support SA when A2 ≡ −1 (mod p). By
   establishing the functional equation PA (AX) + A · PA (X) = AX and inter-
   preting it as a covariance relation on the quotient space Fp [X]/(GSA (X)), we
   prove that the digit-extraction polynomial admits the structured factoriza-
   tion PA (X) = 12 X + X 3 Q(X 4 ), reducing the effective Paterson–Stockmeyer
   degree by a factor of 4. We further establish that the resulting term count
                               Order-Four Symmetry in BGV Bootstrapping           5

   (|SA | − 1)/4 + 1 is tight via Schur’s lemma, confirm global optimality of
   A = 256 via exhaustive search, and prove a multiplicative interaction theorem
   with asymmetric BSGS [24] yielding an additional r1/t key-switch reduction.
2. First concrete O(log D) linear-transform instantiation for non-power-
   of-two cyclotomics. We provide a new construction for homomorphic linear
   transforms on the standard HElib parameter set (m = 50731 = 97 × 523).
   Our approach identifies the number-theoretic condition D | pd − 1 as the key
   enabler for a mixed-radix Cooley–Tukey butterfly factorization with slot-field
   twiddle factors. For the dominant D = 96 block, this reduces automorphisms
   from 18 (BSGS) to 11 per cascade (−39%). We validate correctness via Rader’s
   algorithm on the actual slot ring Fp18 and analyze the practical interaction
   with HElib’s BSGS framework, and we additionally provide a first encrypted
   prototype of the butterfly transform on the full ring, correct on all 2784 slots,
   whose wall-clock advantage over BSGS emerges at larger block dimensions
   (D = 576).
3. Implementation and comprehensive evaluation. We implement both
   optimizations in HElib and conduct extensive evaluations at the recommended
   operating points of Section 6.1. On the NTT-friendly set (p = 65537, m = 216 ,
   32768 slots) the results demonstrate a 1.85× digit-extraction speedup and a
   1.27× total thin-bootstrapping speedup over the Ma et al. baseline, while
   the three stages the contribution does not touch move by at most one per
   cent. Beyond this headline set the filter is validated on nineteen encrypted
   parameter sets with 1297 ≤ p ≤ 65537, always against the state-of-the-art Ma
   et al. baselines [16,17]: the digit-extraction speedup ranges over 1.72–1.88×
   on general cyclotomic rings (37637 ≤ m ≤ 65047) and 1.84–2.13× on the
   power-of-two ring m = 216 . Both optimizations are drop-in compatible with
   existing implementations and compose with orthogonal techniques including
   subring secret encapsulation and homomorphic NTT.
1.3   Techniques Overview
Briefly, our approach exploits algebraic structure in the digit-extraction poly-
nomial and the slot-field arithmetic of non-power-of-two cyclotomics to reduce
both dominant bootstrapping costs simultaneously. We first construct a char-
acter structured digit extraction polynomial with reduced effective evaluation
degree, then provide a concrete butterfly decomposition for the homomorphic
linear transforms. Since the two optimizations target different stages and lever-
age different algebraic tools, we present each separately.

2.3   BGV Thin Bootstrapping
As homomorphic computations progress, ciphertext capacity decreases until no
further operations can be performed correctly. Bootstrapping restores capacity
by homomorphically evaluating the scheme’s own decryption circuit on the input
ciphertext ct = Encs′ (m; pr ), producing a fresh ciphertext with reduced noise.
    The original BGV bootstrapping of Halevi and Shoup [13], known as fat
bootstrapping, operates on fully packed ciphertexts where each slot stores an
extension field element in Zpr [ζ] with [Zpr [ζ] : Zpr ] = d. After the CoeffToSlot
step, the d coefficients of each slot element must be unpacked into d separate
ciphertexts, and digit removal is applied independently to each one. This d-fold
                              Order-Four Symmetry in BGV Bootstrapping          9

replication multiplies both the number of polynomial evaluations and the number
of linear transforms by a factor of d, making fat bootstrapping prohibitively
expensive when the slot extension degree is large (e.g., d = 18 for m = 50731).
    In 2018, Chen and Han [4] observed that when each slot stores only a scalar
in Zpr (i.e., d = 1), the unpacking step is eliminated entirely and digit removal
is applied to a single ciphertext. This thin bootstrapping procedure, illustrated
in Figure 1, consists of four steps:
– SlotToCoeff: Move the slot values into the powerful-basis coefficients via a
  homomorphic linear transform, producing an encryption of a plaintext poly-
  nomial m ∈ Rpr .
– Decryption formula simplification and inner product: Perform mod-
  ulus switching and key switching to obtain (b, a) ∈ R2 satisfying pwfl(b +

  under plaintext modulus pe .
– CoeffToSlot: The inverse linear transform moves the powerful-basis coeffi-
  cients back into slots. Each slot now contains an integer pe−r mi + ϵi ∈ Zpe .

  pe−r mi +ϵi by removing the lower p-adic digits, recovering the original message

2.4   Bounded-Support Digit Extraction
The digit-extraction problem is: given w = pe−r mi + ϵi ∈ Zpe with |mi | < pr /2
and |ϵi | ≤ B, recover mi by homomorphically evaluating a polynomial that
removes the lower p-adic digits. The classical digit-extraction polynomial Ge (X)
has degree (p − 1)(e − 1) + 1, which is prohibitively large for large primes p.

For non-power-of-two cyclotomics, the homomorphic√linear transforms (Slot-
ToCoeff/CoeffToSlot) rely on generic BSGS with O( D) automorphisms per

    In this section, we provide the first concrete instantiation of the Peikert–
Pepin framework for the standard HElib non-power-of-two parameter set (m =
50731 = 97 × 523). Our contribution is the identification of the number-theoretic
condition D | pd − 1 as the concrete enabler, the explicit mixed-radix butterfly
algorithm with precomputed slot-field twiddle factors, and the plaintext-level
validation of correctness and operation count. In addition to the plaintext-level
validation, we provide a first encrypted prototype of the butterfly transform
on the full ring m = 50731: the complete dimension-96 CoeffToSlot chain runs
on ciphertexts and decrypts correctly on all 2784 slots, consuming 194 bits of
capacity over its 41 automorphisms (17 hoisting classes) with no overflow even
at a 600-bit budget. Its wall-clock advantage over BSGS emerges only at larger
block dimensions (D ≈ 576); the per-dimension measurements are in the artifact.

7   Conclusion
We presented two algebraic optimizations for large-prime BGV bootstrapping: an
order-four character filter that exploits A2 ≡ −1 (mod p) to force the structured
factorization PA (X) = 12 X + X 3 Q(X 4 ), reducing the effective PS degree by 4×
with provable tightness, and the first concrete O(log D) butterfly instantiation
for non-power-of-two cyclotomics, validated on the standard HElib parameter set.
On the recommended power-of-two configuration (p = 65537, m = 216 , 32768
slots), our single-threaded implementation cuts digit-extraction cost by 1.85×
30      Z. Xiong et al.

and whole recryption by 1.27×; measured across nineteen encrypted sets span-
ning both ring families and the 80- and 128-bit levels, digit extraction speeds up
by 1.72× to 2.13× while the stages the method does not touch move by at most
one per cent. Both optimizations are drop-in replacements that compose with
subring encapsulation, homomorphic NTT, and other orthogonal techniques.
   Future directions include subring integration for cascading degree reduction,
extended key infrastructure for asymmetric BSGS, and higher-order character
groups where ord(A) > 4 is feasible.
